mesoscaleDiscussions.summary: The threat for very large hail and severe winds will continue as a robust supercell migrates southeast across western South Dakota

details.label: Summary
details.text: The threat for very large hail and severe winds will continue as a robust supercell migrates southeast across western South Dakota

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Over the past hour, a lone, but intense, supercell has exhibited persistent three-body scatter spikes consistent with very large hail, and has also produced wind gusts of at least 61 mph per recent reports. More recently, the reflectivity core has diminished slightly, and the storm motion has shifted from due south to southeasterly, suggesting a slight weakening of the storm's internal pressure perturbations and overall intensity. However, this cell will continue to reside within an environment very favorable for intense convection (MLCAPE near 4000 J/kg and nearly 50 knots of effective bulk shear as sampled by the 00 UTC UNR and ABR soundings), so some degree of re-intensification appears possible. Additionally, new updraft development is noted on the western flank of the cell, which may also intensify and pose a threat for very large (2 inch) hail and severe gusts. Given the elongated/straight nature of regional wind profiles, the emergence of this new cell hints that cell interactions and cold pool amalgamation may increase over the next couple of hours as the new cell begins to split. This may result in a very gradual transition from a supercellular to a clustered/linear storm mode with an attendant increase in severe wind potential as storms move further south/southeast. A few recent high-res solutions hint at this transition, but confidence in this scenario is somewhat limited at this point due to the isolated nature of the convection

details.label: Most probable threats
details.text: MOST PROBABLE PEAK TORNADO INTENSITY...UP TO 90 MPH · MOST PROBABLE PEAK WIND GUST...65-80 MPH · MOST PROBABLE PEAK HAIL SIZE...1.50-2.50 IN

mesoscaleDiscussions.summary: An isolated threat for severe hail/wind continues this evening across parts of southern Arizona

details.label: Summary
details.text: An isolated threat for severe hail/wind continues this evening across parts of southern Arizona

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Convection has tended to focus/spread slowly westward across southern AZ this evening, with modest (15-20 kt) easterly mid-level flow present on recent VWPs from KEMX. A measured severe gust to 66 mph was observed to the east of KTUS with a small cell, and any ongoing convection should also be capable of producing isolated severe gusts given the very well mixed boundary layer observed on the 00Z PHX sounding. In fact, modifying this sounding for the latest surface observations at KPHX (105/60F) suggests that minimal MLCIN is present at the moment. Still, given a dearth of upstream convection over the Mogollon Rim, appreciable severe wind risk in the near term will probably tend to remain fairly isolated and confined to parts of southern AZ with ongoing convection. Occasional hail may also occur with the strongest cores

details.label: Most probable threats
details.text: MOST PROBABLE PEAK WIND GUST...55-70 MPH · MOST PROBABLE PEAK HAIL SIZE...UP TO 1.25 IN

mesoscaleDiscussions.summary: Convection developing in eastern Iowa will likely intensify in the coming hours and could pose some severe threat for portions of eastern Iowa into northern Illinois. Confidence in exact evolution is limited, but watch issuance may need to be considered

details.label: Summary
details.text: Convection developing in eastern Iowa will likely intensify in the coming hours and could pose some severe threat for portions of eastern Iowa into northern Illinois. Confidence in exact evolution is limited, but watch issuance may need to be considered

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Latest regional reflectivity and GOES IR imagery shows steady deepening of nascent convection across eastern IA along a diffuse warm frontal zone. A recent 00 UTC DVN RAOB sampled weak mixed-layer inhibition that is evidently being overcome by ascent within the frontal zone as a nocturnal jet slowly strengthens. This sounding also sampled extreme buoyancy and adequate deep-layer wind shear for organized convection. Consequently, it seems likely that further intensification will occur over the next 1-2 hours. Moderate veering through the lowest 3 km is also noted in the observed hodograph, which should support the potential for a supercell or two capable of producing large hail and perhaps brief tornadoes. The primary uncertainty regarding this potential is the possibility of destructive storm interactions and clustering given forecast storm motions largely along the zone of initiation. This potential is hinted by recent solutions of the HRRR and RRFS, which show initially semi-discrete cells growing upscale into northern IL later this evening. Convective trends will continue to be monitored, and watch issuance may be needed if robust supercells become more imminent

details.label: Most probable threats
details.text: MOST PROBABLE PEAK TORNADO INTENSITY...85-110 MPH · MOST PROBABLE PEAK WIND GUST...55-70 MPH · MOST PROBABLE PEAK HAIL SIZE...1.00-1.75 IN
